next_phase_scope: Phase 5C corrective shadow-retrieval evaluation and controlled contextual-usefulness review. The original PPR result remains a preserved FAIL; v2 may execute only under its frozen metric contract. Contextual retrieval remains disabled by default, explicitly human-gated, and without action authority. Phase 5D execution remains blocked pending executable fixtures, deterministic receipts, runtime fingerprints, and per-arm approvals.

items.description: Local summarizer performance and suitability are hardware-sensitive; Nemotron exhausted RAM and neither tested local model produced an accepted candidate.
items.current_mitigation: No local candidate is approved; extractive-v1 remains available and model-backed Compact Memory remains shadow-only.
items.exit_criteria: A preregistered local benchmark passes provider contract and retention gates on explicitly recorded target hardware without resource exhaustion.

items.description: The cloud-first model path introduces provider availability, network, latency, cost, and external-service dependency.
items.current_mitigation: Explicit CLOUD opt-in, call-time authorization, official HTTPS endpoint restriction, no hidden fallback, shadow-only generation, and extractive baseline preservation.
items.exit_criteria: An approved operational dependency policy defines availability, privacy, cost, fallback, and human stop conditions, or a validated local provider removes the dependency.

items.description: The human-reviewed retention corpus is balanced but small, synthetic, and reviewed in a single adjudication round.
items.current_mitigation: Claims are limited to the frozen corpus; protected-category gates and human review are mandatory.
items.exit_criteria: A larger approved corpus with multiple reviewers, disagreement handling, bilingual and adversarial cases passes preregistered thresholds.

items.description: Long-horizon Compact Memory drift beyond 200 independent cumulative updates has not been characterized.
items.current_mitigation: No summary-of-summaries, full regeneration remains possible, provenance is revalidated, and live prompt injection is disabled.
items.exit_criteria: Preregistered repeated-run and sequential-update tests establish drift, correction, forgetting, provenance, storage, and latency bounds beyond 200 updates.

items.description: Provider-switch continuity has unit coverage for state non-mutation but lacks deep semantic continuity testing over extended histories.
items.current_mitigation: Provider identity is stamped and validated; JOI owns state and source evidence; switching providers does not transfer memory ownership.
items.exit_criteria: Cross-provider round-trip, restart, correction, forgetting, and long-history tests meet one frozen semantic and provenance contract.

items.description: Recovery from a live provider outage during memory generation has not been exercised against a real provider failure sequence.
items.current_mitigation: Unit tests preserve previous manager state and prohibit saves after provider failure; no hidden retries or fallback are allowed.
items.exit_criteria: Deterministic outage tests cover connection loss before, during, and after generation, restart recovery, no partial writes, continued conversation, and auditable operator-visible errors.

items.description: API budget, request-rate, concurrency, and rate-limit stop controls do not have a formal approved policy.
items.current_mitigation: Token use and estimated cost are recorded; cloud and provider activation require explicit configuration.
items.exit_criteria: An approved policy and tests enforce per-run and period budgets, rate/concurrency limits, fail-closed behavior, and human-visible exhaustion state.

items.description: API key rotation, revocation, expiry, and post-revocation behavior have not been tested end to end. The key exposed from the ignored local .env during the closure scan was subsequently revoked and replaced.
items.current_mitigation: Provider-specific restricted replacements are stored as user-scoped Windows DPAPI records outside the repository. Settings and core are credential-blind; adapters retrieve only their own credential after CLOUD and official-endpoint validation, deny redirects, suppress secret-bearing exception chains, and emit content-free access audits. The former keys were revoked/deleted, both replacements passed one-request identity checks, and both dashboards showed no unexpected activity, usage, or cost.
items.exit_criteria: Rotation and revocation tests prove no secret persistence, fail-closed calls, operator-visible status, safe recovery with a replacement key, and auditability.

items.description: Partial corruption and recovery of candidate, report, manifest, and durable Compact Memory artifacts need adversarial validation.
items.current_mitigation: Malformed, stale, invalid-UTF-8, and interrupted runtime Compact Memory artifacts are uniquely quarantined with content-free SHA-256 receipts; restart recovers to empty derived state. Frozen manifests are verified read-only by path, size, and SHA-256 and are never repaired or moved.
items.exit_criteria: Adversarial truncation, bit-flip, missing-file, mismatched-manifest, interrupted-write, quarantine, restore, and restart tests pass without silent recovery or partial publication.

items.description: Provenance consistency across multiple external providers has not been tested.
items.current_mitigation: JOI validates source turn IDs, policy IDs, provider identity, model identity, and the complete candidate independently of provider confidence.
items.exit_criteria: At least two approved providers pass identical frozen provenance, correction, forgetting, identity-mismatch, and provider-switch tests.

items.description: Memory schema migrations lack a durable versioned upgrade, compatibility, rollback, and recovery strategy.
items.current_mitigation: Unknown schema versions are rejected and legacy candidates remain readable; no implicit migration is performed.
items.exit_criteria: A documented migration contract with fixtures and tests proves forward upgrade, backward compatibility boundaries, rollback, interrupted migration recovery, provenance preservation, and audit logs.

items.description: Provider credentials excluded from Git were stored as plaintext in an ignored project-tree .env that remained readable by local tooling and processes.
items.current_mitigation: The plaintext project-tree .env was removed. Recursive workspace, environment, and shell-history scans found no live credentials. Separate restricted OpenAI and ElevenLabs replacements are stored in user-scoped DPAPI records outside the repository and resolve only through CredentialProvider at authorized call time. Both former keys were revoked/deleted; both replacements passed identity checks; dashboards showed no unexpected activity, usage, or cost.
items.exit_criteria: No provider credential exists as plaintext inside the project tree; recursive workspace and publishable scans pass; settings, exceptions, timeouts, redirects, subprocess failures, diagnostics, and memory artifacts contain no key; CLOUD OFF performs no credential access; DPAPI set/get/delete/restart and controlled provider smoke tests pass; old credentials are confirmed revoked; new restricted credentials work only through CredentialProvider; full regression, JSON validation, diff hygiene, and durable-state checks pass.
